facts.detail: A reported total loss of service that remains unrepaired after two full working days attracts £10.34 for each calendar day under the scheme.
A missed engineer appointment, or cancellation with less than 24 hours notice, attracts £32.31.
A promised new-service start that is missed attracts £6.46 for each calendar day of delay.
Automatic-compensation amounts increase annually in line with inflation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compensation rates are customer-remedy evidence and do not prove parcel coverage, technology or measured speed.

facts.detail: The scheme covers residential fixed broadband and landline products supplied by signatories.
Unless otherwise agreed, compensation is credited no later than 30 calendar days after resolution, termination, cancellation or the missed appointment.
For loss of service the customer reports the fault; qualifying delayed-repair payments then start automatically.
Home equipment or activity, contract breach, customer-caused failure or customer obstruction can exclude payment.

guard_streams.write_limit: Scheme eligibility and payment do not establish the physical cause or exact location of a network fault.

facts.detail: Providers serving consumers, small businesses up to ten employees and small not-for-profits must maintain compliant complaints procedures and belong to ADR.
The complaints code must be accessible and provide phone, postal and email or webform contact routes.
The code must describe investigation steps, resolution timeframes, outcomes and ADR escalation.
Providers must take prompt, active steps and promptly communicate the outcome.

guard_streams.write_limit: A complaints process record is customer-service evidence, not parcel coverage or performance.

facts.detail: ADR schemes independently and impartially assess evidence from the customer and provider and are free for customers.
An unresolved complaint can be taken to ADR after at least six weeks.
A deadlock letter permits ADR access before the six-week point.
Ofcom currently approves CISAS and Communications Ombudsman for telecoms ADR.

guard_streams.write_limit: ADR eligibility and outcomes cannot alter an individual parcel's network-confidence score.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom ADR schemes performance updated 23 July 2026

facts.detail: Communications Ombudsman reported 95% of calls answered within two minutes in Q2 2026.
Communications Ombudsman reported 99% of case decisions within six weeks in Q2 2026.
CISAS reported 99% of calls answered within two minutes in Q2 2026.
CISAS reported 97% of case decisions within six weeks in Q2 2026.

guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly ADR KPIs are scheme-level service metrics and cannot be applied to parcel availability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom social tariffs guide updated 22 June 2026

facts.detail: Social tariffs target households receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit and specified other benefits.
A household with a Universal Credit claimant can switch to any tariff for which the published conditions are met.
The person receiving the qualifying benefit needs to be the main person on the contract.
Some providers also accept benefits such as Personal Independence Payment or Attendance Allowance.

guard_streams.write_limit: Benefit eligibility and tariff availability are affordability evidence, not exact network coverage.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom social tariffs guide updated 22 June 2026

facts.detail: The published social-tariff price range is £10 to £24 per month.
Most listed tariffs offer unlimited superfast broadband above 30 Mbit/s.
Where the current provider offers a social tariff, an eligible customer can switch to it at any time without a charge.
Published social-tariff protections include no early-exit fee and no mid-contract price increase.

guard_streams.write_limit: Advertised tariff speed and price are contractual offers, not measured parcel speed or serviceability.

facts.detail: The pounds-and-pence price-rise rules took effect on 17 January 2025.
New consumer contracts cannot include inflation-linked or percentage-based in-contract price-rise terms.
Any written-in increase must be stated upfront in pounds and pence.
The increase and its timing must be presented prominently and transparently at the point of sale.

guard_streams.write_limit: Price-rise disclosure is contract evidence and cannot populate parcel price, coverage or speed fields.

facts.detail: If the contract does not specify the increase and the provider raises the price, at least 30 days notice is required.
The same notice and exit protection applies when the provider raises price above the contracted amount.
The customer receives 30 days to exit without an exit fee.
An eligible customer should be able to move to the provider's social tariff without a penalty even while in contract.

guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer exit rights and tariff switching do not prove current network availability.

guard_streams.source: DSIT Very Hard to Reach alpha trials

facts.detail: The alpha trials assess low Earth orbit satellite delivery of high-speed, low-latency broadband.
The programme covers more than a dozen very-hard-to-reach locations.
The trial premises are among the less than one percent that may be too difficult to upgrade using physical cables.
The trials also assess supplier, distributor and project-partner capabilities.

guard_streams.write_limit: A technology trial at selected sites cannot be promoted as national or parcel-level commercial coverage.

facts.detail: The evaluation plan covers the Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy and Gigabit Broadband Voucher Scheme.
GIS contracts subsidise network providers where gigabit deployment is not commercially viable.
GBVS provides vouchers worth up to £4,500 toward installation of gigabit-capable networks.
GigaHubs for public-sector buildings are covered by a separate BDUK Hubs evaluation plan.

guard_streams.write_limit: Evaluation mechanisms and intended impacts are programme evidence, not completed parcel connections.

facts.detail: The NR OMR gathers suppliers' existing and planned broadband build over the next three years.
The process aims to avoid subsidy intervention that disrupts credible commercial build plans.
BDUK combines Connected Nations, public supplier information and supplier submissions when forming intervention areas.
Project Gigabit subsidy supports residential and business broadband networks, not leased-line connections.

guard_streams.write_limit: OMR classification and planned build are subsidy-planning evidence, not current parcel serviceability.

guard_streams.source: Closure of May 2026 National Rolling OMR

facts.detail: The May 2026 NR OMR closed at 5pm on 1 June 2026.
The next NR OMR is due in September 2026 under the January-May-September cycle.
Submitted data and evidence are formally assessed for England and Wales.
BDUK states that postcode- and UPRN-level outputs will be published after evaluation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Announced future outputs and supplier submissions must not be treated as accepted current coverage data.

guard_streams.source: BDUK delivery performance Q2 2026 announcement and July management table

facts.detail: The quarterly official statistics measure premises receiving gigabit-capable coverage as a result of BDUK subsidy.
The April-to-June 2026 statistical release is scheduled provisionally for August 2026 and was not yet available at this run.
The July contract-management table is not directly comparable with official statistics.
July management figures are rounded to the nearest ten and subject to variable ingestion lag.

guard_streams.write_limit: A future statistics release and rounded management data cannot populate exact parcel outcomes.

guard_streams.source: BDUK July 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress

facts.detail: The July table is a snapshot of BDUK data held on 16 July 2026.
Call-off one reports 60,180 contracted and 17,170 built contracted premises.
Suffolk reports 38,350 contracted and 18,560 built contracted premises.
North Oxfordshire reports 4,180 contracted and 3,860 built contracted premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract-level rounded snapshots do not identify current address readiness or orderability.
